summary: Lebanon County, PA: register lists a wooden tower site; four wooden towers were removed in 1954 and a concrete observation tower built that year still stands in Clarence Schock Memorial Park.

facts.name_origin: Governor Dick was the nickname of a wood chopper and charcoal burner who labored for nearby Cornwall Furnace (1994 article)
facts.earlier_use: The first tower at the site was a geodetic survey signal station (1994 article)
facts.later_owner: SICO Corp. founder Clarence Schock later acquired the land (1994 article)
facts.design: Register: wooden tower. 1994 article: four 50-foot wooden towers, removed 1954
facts.status_note: Wooden towers removed in 1954. A concrete and steel observation tower built in 1954 still stands on the hill; sources call it an observation tower, not a fire lookout

access.note: Clarence Schock Memorial Park; trails open dawn to dusk (LebTown, 2019). A 1994 article says the land is preserved for public use.

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 miles one way to the observation tower (UncoveringPA); the park has 14 miles of trails (LebTown)

events.note: Coleman narrow-gauge railroad to the summit looped around the first wooden observatory (1994 article)
Tower House, a summer home for the Schocks, completed (LebTown)
Schock had the four wooden towers removed after vandalism. Whether the register's wooden tower was one of them is unconfirmed.
New concrete and steel observation tower built in the old railroad loop; sources read describe it as standing
Schock donated the property to the former Mount Joy School District, now Donegal (1994 article)
Tower House torn down for safety; only parts of its foundation remain (LebTown)
Donegal School District ceded ownership to the SICO Foundation and Lebanon County
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's wooden tower is no longer standing, but a concrete observation tower built in 1954 still stands on the hill. The register calls the site a fire-tower site; Rambles describes the wooden towers as part of a nature park. The sources do not clearly match, so the link is unconfirmed.

sources.title: Photo story: taking a fall foliage hike up to Governor Dick Observation Tower

notes_for_editor: The register's wooden tower is not clearly identified. Rambles (1994) describes four 50-ft wooden towers erected by Clarence Schock and removed in 1954, but it does not call them fire lookouts; the register's tower may be one of them, unconfirmed. The concrete tower (66 ft, built 1954) is called an observation tower by the sources and is still standing; it is not a lookout. The record's status 'gone' is right for the wooden tower only, so the status note explains the standing tower. The 1994 and 2019 sources are the only current descriptions read; no current park page was checked. Do not encourage climbing; the story only notes the public trail and the tower as a destination.
